enonce_intro_markdown:
A continuous random variable $X$ has probability density function, $f$, defined by

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{16}\,x(kx + 12), & 0 \le x \le 2 \\ 0, & \text{elsewhere.} \end{cases}$$
incertitudes: Question 5 (a) : le sujet imprime $f(x) = \frac{1}{16}x(kx+12)$ ; la normalisation donne $k = -3$ (négatif), et $f(x) = \frac{3}{16}x(4 - x) \ge 0$ sur $[0, 2]$ : la densité est valide. Le résultat à démontrer en (d), $m^3 - 6m^2 + 8 = 0$, confirme cette lecture de l'énoncé.

questions.enonce_markdown: Find (a) the value of the constant $k$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A probability density function integrates to 1 over its range:

$$\int_0^2 \frac{1}{16} x(kx + 12)\,dx = \frac{1}{16}\int_0^2 (kx^2 + 12x)\,dx = \frac{1}{16}\left[\frac{kx^3}{3} + 6x^2\right]_0^2 = \frac{1}{16}\left(\frac{8k}{3} + 24\right) = 1$$

$$\frac{8k}{3} + 24 = 16 \;\Longrightarrow\; \frac{8k}{3} = -8 \;\Longrightarrow\; k = -3$$

**$k = -3$**, so $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{16}x(12 - 3x) = \dfrac{3}{16}x(4 - x)$, which is non-negative on $[0, 2]$ as a density must be.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Show that

(d) the median, $m$, of $X$ satisfies the equation $m^3 - 6m^2 + 8 = 0$
questions.corrige_markdown:
The median $m$ is defined by $P(X \le m) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, that is $\displaystyle\int_0^m f(x)\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}$, with $0 < m < 2$. Using $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{16}(12x - 3x^2)$:

$$\int_0^m \frac{12x - 3x^2}{16}\,dx = \frac{1}{16}\left[6x^2 - x^3\right]_0^m = \frac{6m^2 - m^3}{16} = \frac{1}{2}$$

$$6m^2 - m^3 = 8 \;\Longrightarrow\; m^3 - 6m^2 + 8 = 0 \qquad \blacksquare$$

(Check: the cubic has three real roots, approximately $-1.064$, $1.305$ and $5.759$. Only $m \approx 1.305$ lies in $[0, 2]$, so it is the median.)
